svg.text: The painless eye and the painful eye
Two of Ghana's leading causes of blindness. One steals vision quietly; one announces itself and must be treated the same hour.
Cataract — clouding of the lens
Painless. Vision blurs over months or years.
Glare from headlights and sunlight. Colours fade.
The pupil may look grey or white.
Reversible: surgery restores the sight.
The barrier in Ghana is not the operation but
reaching it — distance, cost, fear, and the belief
that failing sight is a normal part of growing old.
Glaucoma — pressure damaging the nerve
Chronic form: painless, takes the edges of vision
first, so it is noticed only when it is advanced.
Acute form: severe eye pain, headache, vomiting,
a red eye, haloes around lights, hazy cornea,
and a fixed mid-dilated pupil.
Not reversible: sight already lost does not return.
Acute glaucoma is a same-hour emergency.
The question that separates them at the door
Does the eye hurt, and did the vision change suddenly? Gradual and painless can wait for a clinic
appointment. Sudden, painful, red, or a sudden loss of vision must be seen today — that list also includes
chemical splash, penetrating injury and a curtain falling across the vision.
After eye surgery, the danger is pressure and infection
Teach the patient not to rub the eye, not to bend below the waist, not to lift heavy loads, and not to strain
at stool. Report at once: increasing pain, discharge, or vision that is getting worse rather than better.
